subject: QBR readout prep & dependency index
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR readout prep & dependency index

Thanks team — quick follow-up from today’s cross-functional sync. We covered the high-level readout for Orion Health and surfaced three dependencies that could block the QBR-ready narrative if unresolved. I’ve captured the asks below and noted who I expect to own next steps. Please confirm or update ownership by EOD tomorrow so I can lock the exec slide.

Summary of asks (short):
- Integration latency baseline: need a firm SLA from Cloud vendor + test plan (owner: Vivek).
- Billing demo data: product to provide anonymized sample flows for cost-per-call calc (owner: Marissa).
- QBR slide + topline: compile 2-slide story + 1 backup slide showing fallback behavior (owner: Grace / Laura to support).

Immediate next steps:
1) Vivek: reach out to CloudVendor contact for capacity SLA and share by Thu 5/20.
2) Marissa: drop anonymized demo dataset and call samples to the shared doc (link below) by Wed EOD.
3) Karthik: finalize the one-line exec ask phrasing so leadership can pre-approve (by Wed morning).
4) Laura: validate the two data points we will surface for cost delta (by Thu morning).

Attachments: qbr-readout-draft.md (initial slide outline). I’ll merge inputs into the doc and circulate a v2 by Thu morning.

Related doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B_qbr-readout-draft

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep & dependency index

On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 4:12 PM Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks team — quick follow-up from today’s cross-functional sync. ...

Adding a couple of clarifications and a small ask:
- Exec ask phrasing: propose we keep it tight — "Request: one-time capacity boost + SLA confirmation to secure integration pilot in Q3." Karthik, can you tighten language?
- I uploaded an initial anonymized sample of the billing flows to the shared doc (section: "Sample Flows") — it includes token counts and an example cost calc. Attaching the file I used to build it (qbr-readout-draft.md).

Note on risk: if CloudVendor cannot commit to a hard SLA before the QBR, we should prepare a fallback slide that shows performance on our Dedicated offering (lower latency, higher cost). I flagged that as "fallback" in the doc.

Attachments: qbr-readout-draft.md

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Payments
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep & dependency index

Quick update on the CloudVendor SLA thread — forwarding the response I got this morning. If they can only offer an "up to" SLA (best-effort) rather than a contractual SLA, we need to decide whether to: 1) show the integration as "pilot" in the readout, or 2) switch imagery to Dedicated as the recommended enterprise path.

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Nina Rossi <nina@cloudvendor.io>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:52:00 -04:00
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: SLA request for Orion Health pilot

Hi Vivek,
We can commit to a performance profile with 95th percentile latency targets during peak windows and a capacity reservation option (extra fee). We don't currently provide a contract-level SLA for pilot engagements. Happy to propose a limited-term SLA for the enterprise contract phase.

Best,
Nina
CloudVendor Partnerships


Action for exec slide: Vivek -> recommend we include both outcomes on the slide (pilot: best-effort + capacity add-on; enterprise: contractual SLA on Dedicated). I will also ask Nina for a short summary email we can attach as evidence.

Vivek
Head of Infra Reliability

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR readout prep & dependency index

Thanks all — quick confirm: I updated the exec ask language in the document (one-line, copy below) and added a short dependency index sheet in the drive.

Proposed exec ask (final): "Approve conditional pilot funding and pre-authorize a capacity buffer with CloudVendor to ensure integration performance during customer trials; authorize conversion to Dedicated with contractual SLA if pilot metrics meet thresholds."

I attached an initial dependency_matrix.xlsx (sheet: dependencies -> owners -> mitigation) to the drive and linked it in the qbr-readout doc. Grace: if that works, I’ll mark the items with dates and owners and we can use it directly for the exec slide.

Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B_qbr-readout-draft
